nodes.label: ReportSnapshot (typed JSONB snapshot)
nodes.rationale: A stored PDF is either wrong twice or a second source of truth to keep consistent with the snapshot. Rendering on every download is cheap at this size and means the download endpoint can never serve stale bytes. It also avoids a PHI-bearing PDF sitting on a container filesystem or in a binary column that a routine backup or log scrape could pick up. A report is read once at generation time and never expected to reflect later edits, so a clinician revising a symptom's severity cannot silently rewrite what a report already said.

nodes.label: ReportLab (Platypus) Renderer
nodes.rationale: No new system dependency, a pure-Python-plus-wheel package already validated against Python 3.11. WeasyPrint's Pango/Cairo requirement is a real Windows/Docker cost not worth paying for a two-to-three-page clinical PDF, and a headless-browser render is untestable without a browser in CI. backend/app/reports/renderer.py is a pure function render(snapshot) -> bytes that imports no repository, opens no Session and performs no authorization.

nodes.label: Render Before Persist
nodes.rationale: ReportService.generate_report builds the snapshot, calls the renderer to prove it produces valid PDF bytes, and only then commits the Report row, so a rendering failure raises before any row exists and no partial Report can be found half-rendered. Same guarantee ADR-003 made for the AI pipeline, applied to a smaller surface.

nodes.label: ReportService
nodes.rationale: Composes AnalysisService, VisitService and PatientService rather than querying their tables directly, so a change to any of their authorization rules is inherited automatically.

nodes.label: reports Has No Owner Column
nodes.rationale: analysis_id already resolves to exactly one owning clinician through the analysis to visit to patient chain, and a second independent authorization path would eventually drift from the first. Re-deriving through AnalysisService means a Report's authorization is exactly as correct as Analysis's already-tested authorization. A Report reached by its own id 404s as Report, not as Analysis or Visit.

nodes.label: reports Table
nodes.rationale: Columns: id, analysis_id (FK indexed), generated_by_id (FK to users), generated_at, filename, snapshot (JSONB) plus BaseModel timestamp/soft-delete columns. No pdf_path and no binary PDF column; the empty stub model's design is superseded, not extended.

nodes.label: Filenames Carry No PHI
nodes.rationale: neuroone-report-{report_id}.pdf. The report id is generated in the service rather than left to a database default so the filename is available before the row is constructed.

nodes.label: Multiple Immutable Reports per Analysis
nodes.rationale: Regenerating creates a new row with a new snapshot, mirroring Analysis never overwriting on visit re-run. There is no 'latest report' endpoint because with multiple reports allowed by design 'latest' is ambiguous in a way 'by analysis_id, newest first' is not.

nodes.label: Snapshot Duplication and Retention Exposure
nodes.rationale: A snapshot duplicating Analysis/Visit/Patient/Symptom data is the cost of immutability, not an oversight, and means reports inherits the same retention and authorization sensitivity. A retention or right-to-erasure policy will eventually need to reach reports.snapshot; flagged, not solved.
